Hi friends, it’s Sherrod Brown. I just asked Gabby if I could share an update about my race for the U.S. Senate in Ohio with you.
At the start of the summer, a _Fox News_ poll showed me 8 points ahead of Republican Jon Husted in Ohio. I took this poll with a grain of salt – but still, we were clearly surging ahead in a race that many people once thought was a long shot.
But over the past couple of months, the lies, attacks, and money have ramped up significantly. National Republicans are spending $162 million to defeat me – on top of $3.6 million from tech billionaire Peter Thiel –** and now, a recent poll shows me trailing Husted by 3 points.**
If you thought that the momentum was definitively on our side, this is your wake-up call.
Because what we really have to pay attention to is not just each individual poll, but the polling average of this race. _Right now, it shows me at 47.8% and Husted at 47.2%._
**This race is too close for comfort, and again and again, we’re well within the margin of error. Unless we have the resources to fight back against the GOP and surge ahead, Ohio could have another two years of Jon Husted, and the GOP could stay in control of the Senate until 2029.**
But here’s the good news:
Folks like you have the power to change the outcome of this election and the future of our country.**But it only works if we all get involved.**
The single best thing you can do today to help us flip this seat and take back the Senate from the GOP is make a donation to our grassroots campaign. This is the most competitive and most consequential race in the country, and it will come down to resources. So I’m personally asking:
[**Will you split a donation between my campaign and GIFFORDS PAC today?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-brown-2026.VLItMQ&refcode=em260919-2-b&t=2&akid=11838%2E3935704%2EBkwVIX)

name: Ryan Grim
subject: Drop Site readers showed up
body:
In just a few hours, we've raised the remaining $50,000 needed to support Drop Site contributor Huda Skaik's journey from Gaza to the University of London.

| |
---|---|---
|
# Drop Site readers showed up
### In just a few hours, we've raised the remaining $50,000 needed to support Drop Site contributor Huda Skaik's journey from Gaza to the University of London.
| | | [Nika Soon-Shiong](https://substack.com/@nikasoonshiong)
---
| Sep 19
---
| [](https://substack.com/@nikasoonshiong)
---
Earlier today, we sent you an email asking you to support Drop Site contributor Huda Skaik's journey from Gaza to the University of London.
In just a few hours, we met our goal of $50,000.
Thanks to an extraordinary response from our readers, Huda now has funding to cover her remaining two years of study and will meet the financial requirements of the UK visa process. She wrote:
> "I'm deeply grateful for this opportunity to finally study journalism and experience university life after such a long interruption to my education, and after having to study online due to the ongoing genocide and its aftermath.
> Journalism has shaped me, built me, and given me a reason to keep going. It means so much to me, and it has helped me continue telling stories and being a voice for people whose voices deserve to be heard. I'm especially glad that my voice and my writing have already travelled such long distances before I ever could.
> Thank you for helping make it possible for me to take this next step -- to study, to keep writing, and hopefully to build a life where I can continue doing what I love and what I always wish to."
We'll keep the fundraiser open until Wednesday, September 23. Every additional dollar raised will help with the costs of beginning her studies and building a new life in London.
[Donate to support Huda](https://substack.com/redirect/a745fe57-5f18-467c-a82a-dadcd76ef697?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9ec6dfb1-eb8e-44ce-8133-e05811e1cc06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We also hope you'll consider supporting our ongoing Gaza Journalist Fund, launched last year to help 29 Palestinian journalists cover the costs of shelter, transportation, and basic needs.
Please donate and share the campaign link: [gazafund.dropsitenews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3ee5c5-43ed-49bc-8a77-f22e83eb866f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Our Palestinian colleagues have continued to document the genocide of their people under impossible conditions. We remain guided by the final message of Hossam Shabat: "Do not stop speaking about Gaza. Do not let the world look away."
[Donate to the Gaza Journalist Fund](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3ee5c5-43ed-49bc-8a77-f22e83eb866f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Alongside their donations, supporters' recent messages remind us of what's possible when the community that has formed around Drop Site comes together. As one donor wrote: "Keep the light bright and the message loud."
Thank you.
Nika and the Drop Site team
(C) 2026 Drop Site News, Inc.
Drop Site News Inc., 1930 18th St NW
Ste B2 #1034, Washington, DC 20009

| Fox News agrees with us now
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3155%2E259176%2EeLNZ_o) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3155%2E259176%2EeLNZ_o)_

Hey Peter,

Let's run through the tape real quick:

**The first major play:** I won our primary and became the official Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Iowa.

**The next key move:** Cook Political Report moved Iowa in our direction, citing my strength as a candidate and the energy we've built on the ground.

Then, the big twist: _Fox News_ debuted their first 2026 Senate forecast, **and they rate Iowa a Toss-Up.** [](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/15811?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.20_Turek-Toss-Up_B1_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS2&t=4&akid=3155%2E259176%2EeLNZ_o)

---

I need to tell you about the worst 4 minutes of my life.

Last November, my neighbor's son fell off his bike. Hard.

Head wound. Blood everywhere. The kid was screaming.

His mom was frozen in panic.

I ran over to help...

And realized I had nothing.

No pressure bandages. No trauma supplies. Just some old Band-Aids in a drawer somewhere.

I stood there, helpless, watching a 9-year-old bleed while we waited for the ambulance.

12 minutes felt like 12 hours.

The paramedic later told me: "If that cut had been 2 inches to the left, those 12 minutes could have killed him."

That's when I learned the brutal truth:

The American Red Cross reports that 59% of injury deaths could have been prevented with proper first aid BEFORE the ambulance arrived.

Read that again.

More than half of people who died from injuries would still be alive if someone nearby had been prepared.

And according to the CDC, 44% of Americans don't even have a proper first aid kit in their home.

That ends today.

I spent the last year working with combat medics and EMTs to create something different.

Not another drugstore bandage collection...

But a real trauma kit that handles serious injuries when seconds count.

The 1stHour Trauma First Aid Kit

This is what's inside:

→ Combat tourniquet (stops life-threatening bleeding in seconds)

→ Israeli trauma bandage (battlefield-proven wound compression)

→ Compressed gauze (handles deep wounds)

→ CPR rescue mask (when every breath counts)

→ EMT scissors (cuts through anything)

→ Splint roll, burn gel, emergency blanket

→ Plus 75 more military-grade items

All organized in a compact, waterproof bag.

Normally $139.

Today? Just $49.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDV9AAwAAAAAAw0z60ReODESAM6hZMNfB_QCoilz1ftem9jAwVYzMvU0itRmnQ0mrDW1NayLdfnrC1EvwXnwUcJqyfOl8Wv1uwiU_3kAzmKa5kfeiGS-
Claim Your Trauma Kit at 65% OFF

But here's the catch:

I only have 81 units left at this price.

Once they're gone, this deal disappears forever.

And honestly?

In an emergency, this kit could mean the difference between holding pressure on a wound and watching helplessly.

Between stabilizing an injury and making it worse.

Between a close call and a funeral.

You don't get a second chance to be prepared.

Grab Your Kit Now - Only 81 Left

I still think about that November day.

The kid was fine, thank God.

But I promised myself I'd never be unprepared again.

And I'm here to make sure you don't have to learn this lesson the hard way.

body:
We can’t afford to get this wrong, to move too slow or think too small
#

Peter, this week has made it clear that humanity is being faced with one of the most important challenges of the 21st century. It was also made clear that the Republican Party is completely unprepared to handle it.
Let me break it down for you:
**FIRST:** A researcher at the AI company Anthropic resigned, joining a ton of others who have stepped away out of deep concern for the direction the industry is taking.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sep26.HW03bQ&refcode=em260920-1-90&t=1&akid=4206%2E734936%2E6-S8Gm)
**THEN:** AI CEOs actually agreed with him, and asked the federal government to step in and regulate their industry.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sep26.HW03bQ&refcode=em260920-1-90&t=2&akid=4206%2E734936%2E6-S8Gm)
**NOW:** Donald Trump said no! Seriously. That’s what happened.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sep26.HW03bQ&refcode=em260920-1-90&t=3&akid=4206%2E734936%2E6-S8Gm)
The American people aren’t just afraid AI is coming for their jobs. They think their lives are at risk because that’s exactly what the people running the AI companies are telling them.
This goes beyond politics and corruption, Peter. Donald Trump and the Republican Party do not have a plan right now because they have no idea what they are dealing with. We can’t afford to get this wrong, to move too slow or think too small. And that’s why I’ve already begun working in Congress to treat this with the seriousness it deserves.
But if we’re being honest here, we know there’s no lasting solution to a problem like this if we have a Congress and a President who won’t regulate Big Tech — even when the industry asks them to..
[**If you want to see a Congress that actually tackles problems like this head on and doesn’t shrink from their own responsibilities, chip in $5 towards my work to elect the next generation of leaders. A Democratic majority will not bend the knee to Big Tech.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sep26.HW03bQ&refcode=em260920-1-90&t=4&akid=4206%2E734936%2E6-S8Gm)

body:
We have a snowball’s chance in hell of taking back the U.S. Senate majority without flipping North Carolina’s seat.

[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1337&amount=5&t=8&akid=3529%2E124072%2EZOXIEV)
Now looky here, Peter:
**Democrats have a snowball’s chance in hell of retaking the U.S. Senate majority this fall without flipping North Carolina’s red seat blue.**
Ain’t nobody’s done that since 2008, and right now, the GOP is flooding _beaucoup bucks_ into NC to keep it that way. That’s ‘cause having a proven winner like two-term former Governor Roy Cooper as the Democratic nominee is our best chance of flipping _any_ of the four seats we need.
Roy can’t overcome the full force of the GOP’s dark-money machine on his own, [**_so if you’re my kind of Democrat – the kind who believes our #1 mission is to take back the Senate from Trump’s far-right flunkies – then I’mma need you to get off your derrière and pitch in $5 or more to his grassroots campaign ASAP._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1337&amount=5&t=9&akid=3529%2E124072%2EZOXIEV)
Now you'll have to pardon my French, but I'm scared sh*tless Democrats just don't get how bad we need to fight for North Carolina this year.
Every election since 2008, the polls and expert ratings had us convinced NC was going our way ... only for some milquetoast Republican jackass to beat us by a few points on Election Day.
And believe me: **The jack*ss Roy’s up against this November has _a lot_ going his way.**
His GOP opponent Michael Whatley is the former chair of the RNC, so big-time Republicans like the President and my evil twin Steven Miller are putting their thumbs on the scales in his favor.
On top of that, their super PACs are spending over _$100 million_ so far on baseless attack ads against Roy – **and now, a recent poll shows his slim lead SHRINKING. This race is officially a statistically tied ballgame.**
Without the grassroots resources to surge ahead and reach every last voter between the Outer Banks and the Smokies, Roy could lose this race – and Democrats can say goodbye to flipping the Senate!!!
[**_If you want to stop that from happening, then PLEASE, Peter, before midnight, rush $5 or anything you can spare – _toot sweet_ – to ensure Roy has the grassroots funds to fight back and win in North Carolina. The future of our country depends on it._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1337&amount=5&t=10&akid=3529%2E124072%2EZOXIEV)

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1977, _Happy Days_ aired the infamous episode in which Fonzie, wearing swim trunks and his signature leather jacket, jumped over a caged shark on water skis. The stunt inspired the phrase "[jump the shark](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkE2ynSAQRlejMyxuiz8MGGTi7GWaodVCq_2CYAF6y6w-dbOFLOD76pzz62v-QvYctp94kClrnAO9s6dSKM0uXZvjbOMVyomJc7ocBcp5Bgm9kFqAnNEWvmlWWDuzEgG1NZnXMOpRjwN09W66pVdqXHprO9Av2TnbtwpBa9kpRf1Ss_n8SQ3yJWUHbbOQ7lekcbWDWocRKiXJcYmp-Y4cyk6rf-JNqbHxqL3ZSzlz1f6oYKpg4lAo3Uzv3BTydHPmGNCio-P5DCqYPo4VTK0UD2HKArcoSnT4iDWGP0wCgxM7nucjHD5ZfF_HSU6UnUTeMf2uk3Hnm73n3A-VktuB7P_BlP9seBv4GwAA___reonv)," describing the moment a TV show peaks and begins declining in quality. [See the notorious jump here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0EFygyAUANDT4C4OfjDCgkWnHXdmJqsuHSIf8zMoFjCpt--0V-gF3uJ9DuNgKdA6X-yCpvg4rvjKAUvBNLq0z47yFPe1bDZRTrvDFXMegcP5xPUJ-GinQk8cpa2c8YiAokLTdEorrTpoq7sRQk2tBa07JVt00mpspG7U5BvpRWsrMr8e18AbzlsQ9Q312VtUfuqk7xQwydFRial-RFrLHX044hNTPcWlCuZeypaZeGPQM-iPuJe9viGD_j3roVlObpsHJvpMTHxc9iy-rva4PrKUy_xdJeO2F4VA-dwxyefFUvhzyz87ngZ-AgAA__9uU3SJ). If you recall Saturday mornings as the best part of your childhood, those memories likely involve hours of animated cartoons. For decades, the three TV networks offered a programming combination that started off the weekend on a high note. Today's [_Whatever Happened To ..._](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwVsscjjGHhgqVemUduyIMBz2VcREcLaVt6_SV-j6fdJv-H_f7M1RonX-dHc0HLNd8agJmbHYULY5UPV5W_nhCtWyBVyxVgsS-pMcTyCt80w72s41wUREQNWgOethHMZBw6VZjApOSdRh6M9RY0AIY6fAow_BgZygIfPy5AjyLOUFVDvh2EeHQ_S6i3oA0UkMxLm0P5lWXjCmZ96xtD7fm2QW5kcV6k3AVcD1OI72mTfeJnz9r8WxX4S67kK9dx_P20xfWCfZFBMeB6VEtdeik_PdUfoj-Z8ldgO_AQAA__9uB3Rk) explains why those days are a thing of the past. In case you missed it on _The Flyover Podcast_ , Christopher revealed the six exercises physical therapists actually recommend to their patients. Most people don't notice their strength and balance slipping until something as simple as standing up from a chair gets hard. But when therapists were asked what really works, the same six simple moves came up again and again, and we walked through each one, including one you can do while waiting for your morning coffee. ## States Join Medicaid Discount Plan
President Trump announced on Friday that all 50 states will join the administration's [Medicaid drug-pricing model](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQhZ8Gd6zwrP8oKNK4u2lTWlwYvBNhsGC8Vt4-YqU8QbpPM9LMOd-vr-3LUqS0_7QHGg55S3jXiMxYNl-u3VN1-Up82kK1XB4T1rqBgkkqLUFt1jG9cRts501ABHx2aPp50YteZhi7l0H_HCcPPugAvg9hsXoAFfrefjvf67kj0-4pDapXaoTn4xv1FCwuwc1DmBcQg0JPnMvjd6bELwzxT35jebh8dNG8mM8qnj8ErALW-74fV2012lrA2lDAeuZITK6hLUwuYsN_TfpFwMrlOk7JWdqU8pUcShujHJWsbBmrbN8p7fJAT86Sl82QPAu5zzR7jF0x_rwpRqrTLAa1H5biJyf_p963gb8BAAD__5idkmA), tying the price of select Medicaid drugs to the lowest rates paid in other wealthy nations, which the White House says will save states billions. The plan commits 26 major pharmaceutical companies [_to enact drug pricing for federal agencies_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLEO3CAQRL8Gd5zwnm3sgiIN3aVNaRFYfBthsGDt0_195PxCph3paeb9eq0vR4ny9tPtaDiWNeOnJWTGuoZ6boGaL2fmw1Vq9QyYsbUVFExSLRLU6jzThevgumAiIuCzQ9PreZmXWcPYvY3y6HU_IPZ3AEbttRqnMOnQj4MfOzI3Ty2geqVGeD5-4zJFh3P0eoh6BjEoDMSlPv4UyvzGmL7lwvrwZe-SeTMfTTx_CLACbP4epfFdCbA3WIBViwDbzwLs2eT9UIB1KclRycaOsclysKTMRXI996PJ6K5SMcjsmEpu8nYhj0qe8iZjqXLHQN5REGC7asLxoZSoTVoMatsdpX_b-D-VXgb-BgAA__-REYvb) that match the rates paid in eight other high-income nations, including Canada, Germany, Japan, and the UK. States could save Medicaid $64 billion over the next 10 years, according to a White House Council of Economic Advisers estimate. The model operates through the existing Medicaid Drug Rebate Program and [_focuses on brand-name drugs_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2upDAQBODTQGZkml8HDjaZbDbdEPXYDdO7xkZ2M2hv_8S7wstLpfrqz3N5IgeO22_cycqalkhXCSRCefH53DwXl84oB2Yu-fQUqZQFNIxKGwV6QSf8oaXH2tuVCKirybbTbGYzTzDUbzt30GI3IbbrOPbGuellOj_oWSOZjqBme_dpA7rVeoCueZEZV6R5dVO_TjNUvSbPknLzN3GUN63hf_pQblza62DfIkepul8VPCp4XNfV3IiL6N8dqOAh-dwPtZNnh-zV7VJHZsdxU0fAqDAENWhVBIWK2tkL5V1RICecomqhH_VgoM7WHxeHwGWcql5vO3L4HiE__O5j4SsAAP__YMWFzw). States can choose which eligible drugs they want covered under the model, but must adopt standardized coverage criteria.
## Trump, Xi Prepare for State Visit This Week
U.S. officials [_will greet Chinese President Xi Jinping_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGupCAURL9Gd3TwCggLFrPpXc92lgbh0t4JogG0Z_7-xfcLb1mppFLn_HnNL0eJ8vu329C2uM8ZPzVha1jmUM53oOr3M7fDFarlDJix1hk4KMYNAz473-jCWbg-2IgIOPZoh0kbbfQEsl-t8Ki05CMiaGUGr6UZEExUXuLite7J3nvcAB84lzA-FjQqOtTRTyJOGjrBMVDby-PvTrmtGNP__cLy8PvWJ7u2dtRu_NXBs4OnO26Eu7pDaeQTdvBs5dwO9o-YXyk7VptryC6q1FignLEwLhYwboRFOTEFJ6VTAoIQgxSDDFPsiw3Hh1KiqqZO8PfmKH1faD80d1n4CgAA__9DR4LH) at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday, rather than at the White House, for the first state visit by the leader of China in more than a decade. The visit will include [_an arrival ceremony_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSnSAQRp9GOxxEAS0o0tjdtCmdVRbvZlAcWDXJ02fu_wp_-xXfnHN-veYXUKRj-wk7Og5pPvApEZkxzz5fm6eypuvgEzKVfHk8sJRZSWWEHIWSM6xMN8491N4FRIVdja61wziMg1W6fruwGBy1XG2r-w69hmAAOgUWjdW4Qk3u8ydHJVspteqaBUcTAIew2j7YQVW9RE-ccvM70cFvDPFvujE3a9rr6N7MZ6m6H5WaKjU9z9PwUj4ezYH8WVKOfqF_lZquApWaOF_7Kc4IRxFbRmTxhwRQPlNmATnTDVGkEGgliEW0ujeDNnV2_nwoRirGVr3cdqD4hcDfLHc79T8AAP__RqiGPQ) inside the White House, a Rose Garden military review, and a state dinner. [_A number of key issues_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGupDAQBNDTmIyRaYxtAgebkM2mGyIvbqBXxkZ2M7P_9l_MFX5cpSdV_XnOT0-R0vbbH-h4zXPCd43IjGUO5doC1SVfiU9fqJYrYMJaZ5CgWzm2IGe_ML1wVr4JbkUE7Bt0nbGjHa2BodmdCtbKYI0OPWolA3RdrxejzWB65TtsyN2eHEF2Ug7QP_7iqFePdl2MWo0FoSQG4lwe_zIl3nGNX_mF5bHko4luZz6r6H8JmARMvONOMd6ZgGnPB96TBEw-HJSocvFMOQmYtBwHUF37n9rbrS2X6zjbt687pY0_naa4cL4pRqraCCW3w9PHbviHd70cfAcAAP__2FqAbw) are likely to come up during the visit, including trade, artificial intelligence, and rare earth minerals. U.S. officials said Washington and Beijing may be ready to ease tariffs on some nonstrategic goods. Separately, [_Treasury Secretary Bessent_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI7MQLApXGxDl22i1ZbI4DHMymA0NmTz9095v_DqK12dc_4-xoejSPvy221oS0jjjq8csRTk0fO5eMpzOvdyOKbMp8cdcx5BQSdVL0GNbi504di6ytuACNhUaGttetMbDfdqtQZ770w99cY3Rpm6VdNk6jBrM3UARldkP3-qB1UrdYfmNmHfBYcmzLoN2oBoFXoqiW__Eu1lxRDf6UK-zWmrol1LObJofgkYBAxumj8On03A8OcpYHgR47MkfgsYCp_bIR3xkbjIhRGL_E9yXml3WUZ0Hlk6ZrowyzPLuunuWoNqKrb-eFGMlDstWrVsjuI3QflhuMvCVwAAAP__SLSD_g) will meet over the weekend in New York with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to discuss a range of economic issues.
## LIST: Most Popular Breakfast Cereals by State
Froot Loops is the most popular breakfast cereal in 13 states and [the most-searched cereal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOrCAUgOGnwU6DBxUsKG5jN7fd0pyBwwwbFAPHMfP2m9lX2PpPvuL_uq03jCnuj_-4keWQ152umoiZyurL-fCxunzufGCJtZyedqp1BQlTK-cW5IqO44vWARtvAxGQasj22sxmNhrG5ml7iSAlyuluxqC9ggnUoJzpA2qFemyi_XhyBtlLOYLq7jRPAckEp4egDYhBko-cS_ed485PCumdX1Q6l7cm2SfzUYX6J2ARsFzX1RX_SQIWLBxdIgHLliu3Rz7OhKV1VAhTe3-3lZE_uSnWH1dMKdZJi0E-Nozp1-c_bnlZ-AkAAP__aFV4QQ) in the U.S., according to Google Trends. The tropical-fruit-flavored sugar rings dominate throughout the South, while two relatively healthy options, Cheerios and Rice Krispies, each won five states. Not surprisingly, many state favorites were among [the most sugar-laden options](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L-OszAQBPCngc7ImH-mcPE1dPnaK9EGr8EXY6P1EpS3P-XyCFeO9NNoNF-3-QY--Lj-hx0NuzRHvHJAZqTZ0rlan5d0Rj6AfKbTYsScZyVVL-QolJxhYf_EuYXSGoeosCnR1IMe9agH1ZWbaZuuhUW5HqV1Y6_R6jvWvQOtunoAW3rz7pOjkrWUnWqqO469A9RuGVo3aFW0Eq3nRNV38pE3dOGVnkjVkvYymI35yEXzr1BToabruqodmdIBhJHfplDTJ_i4FmriDcWVKLPI5wr0EgsSQsjCJRIPb7MgiA-04v76CHEgLRAZVhRdL4eSjD0uH4LP_VC0ct3Bh98x_McPn0b9BAAA___t7Iqb). Post Golden Crisp, with 42% sugar by weight, carried Ohio and Indiana. Wheat-based cereals were not so popular. Wheaties, Raisin Bran, and Frosted Mini-Wheats each came out on top in a single state.

**Whatever happened to Saturday morning cartoons?** For a solid three decades, Saturday morning in America meant one thing for kids: wake up before your parents, pour a bowl of something frosted, and park yourself in front of the TV for hours of cartoons. It was appointment viewing before the term existed, and it shaped a generation. Kids memorized [the Saturday morning cartoon schedules](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAYhJ8Gd7bIb8dAQXE6yV3SRKcrEYYfmw2GCHCsvP0qu_sG246-GY2-_xd10T74uFz1hrK6pCIeJWCtmJXN-2J9MWmP9aGzL3m3GLEUBRTGlooWqNKm-ieqQTdWOkTAvkF5YlxwwRmcm1XOQgzczeCo6Bk7z8JyrbGHAZyZObONl-89KoCeKD1D380oRqeRO8MGxziQgaL1NeXuI_lYV3ThlZ6YO5O2Jsi11kch_R8CE4GprtgWXfds9avdUo4-Lq3RuaYUO6ejTdu7R2A6_N0TmG4_sLp8w-pmVrR7wKII8H83dcV6pHwvBP6qkxipagkIAv2kQ3gHQ5OlfRw-BF9GRga6bNqHr3P1l06fEj4DAAD__5U9jdM). Then, gradually, it all went away. The tradition took root in the early 1960s when Hanna-Barbera, the studio behind _The Flintstones_ , _The Jetsons_ , and dozens more, began filling network schedules with made-for-TV animation. By 1966, all three, ABC, NBC, and CBS, were programming full animation blocks between 8 a.m. and noon. Here's a [TV ad promoting CBS' 1965 lineup](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwVsscjjGHhgqVemUduyIMBz2VcREcLaVt6_SV-j6fdJv-H_f7M1RonX-dHc0HLNd8agJmbHYULY5UPV5W_nhCtWyBVyxVgsS-pMcTyCt80w72s41wUREQNWgOethHMZBw6VZjApOSdRh6M9RY0AIY6fAow_BgZygIfPy5AjyLOUFVDvh2EeHQ_S6i3oA0UkMxLm0P5lWXjCmZ96xtD7fm2QW5kcV6k3AVcD1OI72mTfeJnz9r8WxX4S67kK9dx_P20xfWCfZFBMeB6VEtdeik_PdUfoj-Z8ldgO_AQAA__9uB3Rk). What followed was a golden age for kids: _Scooby-Doo_ , _Super Friends_ , _Underdog_ , _Schoolhouse Rock!_ , _The Smurfs_ , and later _G.I. Joe_ , _Transformers_ , and _He-Man,_ a full morning's worth of child-focused entertainment. The whole ecosystem ran on sugar cereal. Kellogg's, General Mills, and Post poured enormous ad dollars into Saturday mornings, [deploying cartoon mascots of their own,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb_GdCAzsNguXLyGbl-bEnnt8TKRwcgeFuXvo02RH0h3i6tzpPNxX-6OEu3P_25DyzEvO141ITOWJZTzGaj6fO58uEK1nAF3rHUBCVMrTQtycZ7phcvommAjIuDQoO2VNtpoBbdmtSGCvukpRGfGXkk_euNNBDV5Y9yjHxqyb540IHspbzB0DzRTdKijV2NUGsQoMRDn0n1m2nnFmL7yC0vn89YkuzIfVQz_BMwC5uu6umslRp_yGer7I2DmfLS9_B2tx4IutZurPnMVMDfFhuOilKhOSozyuTlKPwL-Y5eXhe8AAAD__0XLeI0) who became as iconic to kids as any other TV character. The networks got rich, the cereal companies moved product, and kids got four glorious hours of animation. Everybody won. The decline came slowly, but from multiple directions. Cable channels like Nickelodeon and Cartoon Network began offering cartoons all day, every day, making the once-a-week block less special. VCRs, video games, and weekday syndication pulled viewers away. Then Congress passed the Children's Television Act in 1990, requiring educational programming that squeezed out pure entertainment. NBC dropped its cartoon lineup in 1992. ABC held on through 2011. The very last broadcast block, The CW, signed off on September 27, 2014, and was replaced by a live-action educational lineup. The cartoons themselves live on. In 2024, Weigel Broadcasting [launched MeTV Toons](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO3CAQhJ_G7jhhzNlQUKS57k-b0tqDxd4EwwnWtvL2kfMKfzszGs18v76WL6BEef0JOzqOZcl4tYTMWJdQjzVQ8-XI_IFKrR4BM7a2KKkmIa1QcgHPdOKioQ8uIioce3TDbKyxZlbPfnMKbBwnPRit42DnWXmvwwTBjsaPGkxP7u6TVslByqcaH2-0UwQ00c86zkZ1WmIgLvXxu1DmDWP6W06sD1_2PrmN-dO68UenXp16Xdf18O_2NLfbqdd96JaRVkziXQsED40pr4KLSHBkv4kd-RRcSm4i4yUy8lXqHxEwkAfGcEd9gtbIC8i0A1PJfXXhc1FK1Ka503LdgdL_TfxNlKdT_wIAAP__ynOM2A), a 24/7 network devoted to the classics, from _Bugs Bunny_ to _Scooby-Doo_ to _The Jetsons_. For a solid three decades, Saturday morning in America meant one thing for kids: wake up before your parents, pour a bowl of something frosted, and park yourself in front of the TV for hours of cartoons. It was appointment viewing before the term existed, and it shaped a generation. Kids memorized . Then, gradually, it all went away. The tradition took root in the early 1960s when Hanna-Barbera, the studio behind The Flintstones , The Jetsons , and dozens more, began filling network schedules with made-for-TV animation. By 1966, all three, ABC, NBC, and CBS, were programming full animation blocks between 8 a.m. and noon. Here's a . What followed was a golden age for kids: Scooby-Doo , Super Friends , Underdog , Schoolhouse Rock! , The Smurfs , and later G.I. Joe , Transformers , and He-Man, a full morning's worth of child-focused entertainment. The whole ecosystem ran on sugar cereal. Kellogg's, General Mills, and Post poured enormous ad dollars into Saturday mornings, who became as iconic to kids as any other TV character. The networks got rich, the cereal companies moved product, and kids got four glorious hours of animation. Everybody won. The decline came slowly, but from multiple directions. Cable channels like Nickelodeon and Cartoon Network began offering cartoons all day, every day, making the once-a-week block less special. VCRs, video games, and weekday syndication pulled viewers away. Then Congress passed the Children's Television Act in 1990, requiring educational programming that squeezed out pure entertainment. NBC dropped its cartoon lineup in 1992. ABC held on through 2011. The very last broadcast block, The CW, signed off on September 27, 2014, and was replaced by a live-action educational lineup. The cartoons themselves live on. In 2024, Weigel Broadcasting , a 24/7 network devoted to the classics, from Bugs Bunny to Scooby-Doo to The Jetsons. The shows survived. The ritual didn't. ## Feds to Send Texas $7.5 Billion
The federal government will send Texas $7.5 billion to repay the state for Operation Lone Star, Gov. Greg Abbott [announced Friday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SnDAQhU8jMk21ehhAgQInytapQ0o_rUFlQFRLw-7c3sX6CBt3ff2-9_58zB8ur3l__nYbmfaVyrzTZ12pNeI5UWQ63LuOD19fzOXpGvnC-4yAgwQtEWYXWj5p7l0XjYeoVUdGjZPWgKqHbjGp9zF5dQedHndF_eACYPRDcMqplKjL5noHGkEpQDXdQAeVBj0NYQwhTSh6oJhb4VtbqNGXq2l9l5P4FsrWrWZp7aji_kugFWj_ntldB4H26iLQ-sKRWKC9cgRa0AKtmgTauFTpjoPLSVWO8iF9XtdcdvkfkZXCi3N7S6a8-RdX2mhvMhWW3x4CbccmHp8XVodR9PDcXF6_xdpPBz0N_gsAAP__PGGLTQ). Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed the award, which covers three-quarters of a [$10 billion pot](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkTGOpDAQRU8DmVt2wRg7INiEbDbdEJXtAqw1GNnVzcztV7TmBpt91Zde6en_-Zw_MaZ4rL9xp5G_ljwfdNVEzFTmhUKhE7_r8OHqs5S8IpPL5ZhBghbSCpAzeo4vmntsw-hksKqlUQ3GWgmql-026gC0BNIDLro3YJTuyJohoALXaYttHG-ctCCVkqDMQ1qvFm2N9oP3i4GmlxQi5_LgjZi-sC7pO7-oPHze2zRuzGdtul8NTA1M13U9_r6edJcNTFg4-kQNTLdZA9OZU-To7xj3Pa4FOeZD_LRvvMgn_ZxTPkhUxiLW--ORi1gLrQKdy8yiUNzds1Ta6WAR6MTC77jlnRIeQVTyzxL5W4Tt5oO2wnkMgSgI6s0ietSDMNoHYT4UknadJujaMobziinFqoeml-uOMb19-X93eo3wLwAA__8AYKuY) created in last year's tax-and-spending bill. Texas applied in June. "_Texas held the line when Washington would not_ ," Abbott said. The money still falls short of the $11.1 billion the state says it spent on barriers, buoys, National Guard deployments, and trespassing prosecutions. Democrats uniformly opposed the bill that created the fund. Gina Hinojosa, their nominee for governor, has [pressed Abbott](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3CAQxvGnwR0WEJ8xBUUad5c2pTWYsRcJgzXMrW_fPvJKeYKrpvnrp9H393P5hJRT2f_AgZ6_t7oUvFpGZqRlw0h4wqvZj9C-iOoOjKFSWYwyo1ROGrXAyumJywBd9EFFpzv02k7OKaMH1T08hPiBEKMGO2kEjSboVQ1uDGqzFm2X_M0pZ5TWyuipV27V2-imcbXruk1GDApj4ko9P5DxG9qWX_WJ1K_16LJ_MJ9N_PotzCzMfF1XHypFJMKzEt-RMDPhnmppwsxv4f-VjVPO8oLEqeyyFqm1DCnnVItMRW4YkSBLwnSEL2p4YOEmCTMwRslV1hMJ-M5zLSgbAwkzd-Tjed1OG60Y1H5Ayu9_-ac7P735FwAA__8HUpdl) to collect the money and spend it on household relief. Abbott said Texas is also seeking a share of a separate Justice Department fund to recover the rest.
## UT-Austin Cuts Three Race, Gender Majors
The University of Texas at Austin has [stopped enrolling new students](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHS2yAQhJ8GdXjgol-GgiIN3Z82peYMh0QGSx44JPvtM8orpN6dnW-_39_zN-aSt-UXPsnxO-3zRmcrxEx1ThQrvfDT7l-P1mvdF2R67HWbQcEklZWgZgycD5pHHKJ7qGj1QE7fjbUK9KiG1T2-tElGWa2jwRhH0COmMI0aE9mQ0pDdNacsKK0VaHNTNug0WTOFewjJgBgVxcx7vfFKTG9sqXz2g-ot7M-huJX51cSPnwK8AH-e5y1vLUda87JSpXjVBPjrmQCfMPTCHwE-9Fpz6KVf6cUgwCsrwGsjwHeW2BvnTeKbmmx0UMUiidctB7nQFqnKxj1mavKJf_bahuri68yl5DbdxaiWJ-byD5L_V-7h4G8AAAD__7iskMY) in three majors: African and African Diaspora Studies, Mexican American and Latino Studies, and Women's and Gender Studies. Interim department chair Danielle Clealand told faculty the provost's office rejected their proposal to keep the majors. Students already enrolled can finish their degrees. The university [confirmed the change](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL8GOiNjHMCFi2vocu2VyJg17MVg5N2E5O9PyS9cM81Io3nv5zpeHUbcl2-3geVnSOMOJ0VghjwGmDMc7kXdZaJ7zmlxDFPK-6ikaoU0QsnRecYHjNqVs53kbOoSbN31xkhVa1mudlagQeuuvUzy0qs-mM43jXZdb4JvGyjRvuekUbKupar7Shpfh9b0re-8D70qtIQZOeWKV2B4OgrxlR6QK5-2MtqV-aCi-SrUUKjhPM8qpOeb490XajhSREZPhRoiBEZiMUO8E6adRHAeRAZ_Szvui0g7CLdBRu9ITLgsQCx8ihEWILG52yd_Uxa0uhuI-1FmOx8nxojUdoWWy-Ywfp7xf40-rPoLAAD__3YJjwI) and gave professors until the end of the semester to propose a replacement major. UT [folded seven liberal arts departments into two](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOiPbIRgXLq6hy7VXosVeE0sGo_USkrc_5e4R_nY0Gs33_XnMD0g57etv2NDxO5Z5x6tmZEaaIwbCAz7V3Jd6EpUVGJdC-6ylHoS0QssZPKcXzj20wS0yWNWiU2a0VmrVy_bpNN5vGrUK0kRjMNqohjvgAOOiPBhsk_vOSaulUlKrsZPWqzjYcfDG-zjqppcYEhfq-ImMb6gxf8oLqfNla7N7Mh-1uf1q9NTo6bquLpa3gbNy2r-VRk9fqkZPJ4v_sTioRKy1UBWRzsoEjEEEPIB4w50F5rSlHTiVvQpfcsYVRU4LEmQBxLUlF44r5ZzqYJperhuk_O8R_9Tky-m_AQAA__8KzI1d) in February, citing fragmentation and lopsided student-to-faculty ratios. Roughly 307 students were enrolled across those majors and American studies, under 1% of undergraduates. Julie Minich, a professor of Mexican American and Latino studies, said the cut ends UT's long role in building that field. Texas A&M dropped its women's and gender studies degree earlier this year.
## Court Lets Surrogate-Born Baby Leave Texas
The Texas Supreme Court [refused Thursday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0TD2AFTUGzj7m27pTXAkCCROAJiv_z9KtnV_sCWd0b3Suf8-lq_KJd8v_ykG7v-nbb1zkcr3DvXNXGs_KBXM2ffnrVuF-rst3pfEVBLsBJhpdDzzutEQ3QeolUDO2VmawHVBMPVaTsCwqhHGwgmVimCRjXS2ZOKyaghu_ccWASlANV8AhtU0nbWwYSQZhQTcMx9q6d-5c7f1FJ5bTvXU9huQ3HX3h9NjD8ELgKX4zhORyJ6PwUuVHsOhQUubzKBS-vU3_EzJP8e_4T2fFS-sQzbs3ZZn4Wb9ORfMnLJO1eO8p8HWZh2lp-iwAVnI43XiCOd5VlpLacxjXKO3kibLIKNdgY2Q3XxceRSctNGTHC5US4fjv6__neHvwMAAP__IGWZPw) to stop a California couple from taking their infant son out of Texas for heart treatment in Los Angeles. The court sided with [Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAQhZ_G7oiG8R8UFLdxl9tuaQEeJyjYWDBxkrdfeaV9gq1OcXSOPn1f1-lqQwzb7b9dyfB7SdNGrxKJmfK00Jxpt58ydK48c043y-RS3iYE7AVogTBZz-GgqbX1bBzMWtZk5KC0BpQt1HeDsnFAqlFDMwxz23XOa0ndArio3rZNHcx5BxpBSkCpLqC9XHqtej94vyisWqA5cMoXvhPT25YlftJB-eLTWkdzZ95L1fyrcKxwtM7L5mwqHAun_Dnzl17Y8iiiPPdMKwmfnplF2JjyQRsJbzOJEvxDOOvOndRK9m2vKhzrbOb9FWIMpR-qFm6rDfEHgP8q7jD4HQAA__8El4Ix), the boy's biological parents, over McKenna West, the Alaska nurse who carried and delivered him in Dallas on Aug. 12. Justices wrote that sustaining the child's life was the paramount concern. The boy was born with hypoplastic left heart syndrome and has already had one surgery. West [refused the couple's request](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unTAQhJ_GdEb2hj8XLtLQ3bQp0WKvD9YBjOwFzn37iBR5gdQjfTPz_f6avjCucX_9wo0sf0KadrrLSsyUp0A-04HfpW_ncuacXsg0p7xPoKCTykhQEzqOF00NVt7OyhtdkdX9YIwC3ahqsTgE02OvSDvfGQ1tAPSAvWvnhroWq2gfnDKgtFagh1oZp0Nnhs71zoUBRKPIR0655oWYPljC-p0uyrVLW7Xahfko4sdPAaOA8b7v-j3z5wkFjA9bwKiMgFErAeO_J_JekswUzkJeLniRxDlljmmXWN5FlvPItJF06cws486UL9pJPs2yRPeWO92PDgFjla0_7riusXS9aNRrw7j-ncf_q_Wy8CcAAP__6UCOkg) for an abortion after the diagnosis and traveled to Texas, which bans most abortions, to give birth and seek custody. She says she doesn't trust them to pursue surgery. The couple's lawyers say hospice isn't part of the plan and that doctors have no concerns about their decisions. West has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene.

Greg Abbott . Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed the award, which covers three-quarters of a created in last year's tax-and-spending bill. Texas applied in June. "Texas held the line when Washington would not ," Abbott said. The money still falls short of the $11.1 billion the state says it spent on barriers, buoys, National Guard deployments, and trespassing prosecutions. Democrats uniformly opposed the bill that created the fund. Gina Hinojosa, their nominee for governor, has to collect the money and spend it on household relief. Abbott said Texas is also seeking a share of a separate Justice Department fund to recover the rest. UT-Austin Cuts Three Race, Gender Majors The University of Texas at Austin has in three majors: African and African Diaspora Studies, Mexican American and Latino Studies, and Women's and Gender Studies. Interim department chair Danielle Clealand told faculty the provost's office rejected their proposal to keep the majors. Students already enrolled can finish their degrees. The university and gave professors until the end of the semester to propose a replacement major. UT in February, citing fragmentation and lopsided student-to-faculty ratios. Roughly 307 students were enrolled across those majors and American studies, under 1% of undergraduates. Julie Minich, a professor of Mexican American and Latino studies, said the cut ends UT's long role in building that field. Texas A&M dropped its women's and gender studies degree earlier this year. The court sided with , the boy's biological parents, over McKenna West, the Alaska nurse who carried and delivered him in Dallas on Aug. 12. Justices wrote that sustaining the child's life was the paramount concern. The boy was born with hypoplastic left heart syndrome and has already had one surgery. West for an abortion after the diagnosis and traveled to Texas, which bans most abortions, to give birth and seek custody. She says she doesn't trust them to pursue surgery. body:
The truth is, we’re behind on our fundraising targets. Way behind.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1393&source=&t=1&akid=3629%2E124072%2EMjIxIR) | | | |

Peter – here’s the truth:
**We’re behind on our fundraising targets.** In fact, we’re nowhere near the number of grassroots donations we’ll need to win this race.
We know we ask a lot of this team, but we’re hoping you’ll [**_chip in your first contribution of $5 to help us get back on track today._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1393&amount=5&t=8&akid=3629%2E124072%2EMjIxIR) Let us explain why.
First, it’s not cheap to run a statewide ad campaign and reach voters with our message. With more than 7.8 million registered voters across ten media markets – including two of the most expensive in the United States (Charlotte and Raleigh-Durham) – it can cost as much as $5 million to run an ad.
Second, this will be one of the most expensive Senate races in U.S. history. The GOP’s already spending more than $100 million to defeat us, and since the majority hinges on this seat, experts at Politico say **we can expect to be outspent" substantially more"** between now and Election Day.
Last but not least – President Trump is now personally wading in to tip the scales in our MAGA opponent’s favor. A few days ago, he came to North Carolina for a rally where he told lie after lie about Roy, and a super PAC linked to Trump is currently dumping millions into this race to crush our momentum.
If we don’t see a surge of grassroots support, we’ll have some difficult decisions to make this week.
Because frankly, we're spending money faster than we’re raising it at this point (we only have 44 days left), and we’ll have to spend even more in light of what's coming from the GOP.
**Our only hope is that people like you – who understand the stakes of this race – give what you can to help fill in the gaps. So if flipping North Carolina, retaking the Senate and preventing two more years of unchecked GOP rule matter to you, we have to ask:**
[**_Will you make your first contribution of $5 or more to our grassroots campaign today? We’re short of where we need to be to keep up the fight, and the timing is not great._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1393&amount=5&t=9&akid=3629%2E124072%2EMjIxIR)

clean_body: The truth is, we’re behind on our fundraising targets. Way behind. | | | | | Peter – here’s the truth: We’re behind on our fundraising targets. In fact, we’re nowhere near the number of grassroots donations we’ll need to win this race. We know we ask a lot of this team, but we’re hoping you’ll Let us explain why. First, it’s not cheap to run a statewide ad campaign and reach voters with our message. With more than 7.8 million registered voters across ten media markets – including two of the most expensive in the United States (Charlotte and Raleigh-Durham) – it can cost as much as $5 million to run an ad. Second, this will be one of the most expensive Senate races in U.S. history. The GOP’s already spending more than $100 million to defeat us, and since the majority hinges on this seat, experts at Politico say we can expect to be outspent" substantially more" between now and Election Day. Last but not least – President Trump is now personally wading in to tip the scales in our MAGA opponent’s favor. A few days ago, he came to North Carolina for a rally where he told lie after lie about Roy, and a super PAC linked to Trump is currently dumping millions into this race to crush our momentum. If we don’t see a surge of grassroots support, we’ll have some difficult decisions to make this week. Because frankly, we're spending money faster than we’re raising it at this point (we only have 44 days left), and we’ll have to spend even more in light of what's coming from the GOP. Our only hope is that people like you – who understand the stakes of this race – give what you can to help fill in the gaps. name: Tyler Bowyer, Turning Point Action
subject: You need to see this
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TURNING POINT ACTION (TPACTION
body:
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Friend,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.
---
[](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyUkcGOnDAMhp8m3BgZx4TkwKHSiJ62XfXSY5RJzExUIDQJU_XtK7bzAnv1b3_6bP98s28uLnG7f3Mrj_e07zYX-zcdG3OoqTDXRywWAVULpkWwztf4ZEuuCSM5RUqphsdu0MaABuybx4jagYHeGIMDd7PSs9GKmEDD7LmTTRxPIBiEDglQXhTpXgENEnvskKQg4BBrypdTKXOJgbca3XLxaW2W8VHrXoT8InASOBX2R-aL2zikenYInOp-iqZN4NTTjfV8o_Z267ElYG5N0LKd2ZM0bGQ3GCGnko7s2foUWMjr1-_v7z86SQRGoDrqalcO8ViFvPLq4vIq_h8S8vpwObjyyzr_-xV5t-4u3jchr3V3Hye0vj5faeV8spo8hv1PXJZY1CAI7if7Y8n6yW88R_wXAAD__00pkxE)
---
We're not sitting around waiting on November and hoping everything falls our way. Our teams are already on the ground in these three states, doing the actual work. Knocking doors. Registering voters. Chasing down every conservative ballot until it's counted. Clipboard and tennis shoes work, the kind that doesn't trend online but wins elections. We proved this model in 2024. We ran the most sophisticated ballot-chasing operation the Right has ever put together, and we won every single state where we ran it. 10 for 10. Congress has opened an investigation into waste, fraud, and abuse of federal funds at the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA), the lead agency coordinating L.A. County's homelessness response. Per Just the News, LAHSA has received more than **$1 billion in federal funds since 2021**, including **$220 million in 2024 alone**, yet the agency has struggled to account for how that money was spent. LAHSA reportedly "posed challenges to verifying spending," a central concern of the congressional probe.
**The Nepotism Allegation**
The most prominent accusation centers on former LAHSA CEO Va Lecia Adams Kellum. According to reporting by LAist (cited in the congressional inquiry), Kellum signed a **$2.1 million contract between LAHSA and Upward Bound House**, the nonprofit where her husband worked -- despite having been expected to recuse herself from the transaction due to the conflict of interest. Rep. Tim Burchett, leading the investigation for a House Oversight subcommittee, cited this as evidence of "blatant corruption" and has invited/requested that **Mayor Karen Bass testify** before Congress, given her oversight ties to the agency.

body:
Did you see this?
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=93%2E42639%2Ez5hwpi)
Last week, Vivek Ramaswamy released a video of him trying to hit a baseball in a batting cage while parroting a bunch of far-right talking points.
It was embarrassing, and he pulled it from the internet after getting mocked by Democrats, Republicans, and Independents alike.
Maybe you saw it?
My first thought after seeing it was about youth sports in America.
If you have kids (like me) or grandkids who play youth sports, you know that costs have gone up like crazy over the past few years. Access to the best soccer coaches, facilities, and equipment prices out countless families across the country.
Today in America, the average family is spending about $1,500 per kid on youth sports: basketball, baseball, soccer, dance, and any number of additional sports.
How did this happen?
Private equity rolled up youth sports in an effort to squeeze kids and families for every dollar they could. They buy up facilities, push out the rec leagues, they'll hold tournaments and force families to stay in hotels with expensive rates, they'll charge exorbitant fees to parents who want to just watch their kids play. Once their hooks are in, they have countless ways to extract revenue along the way, turning youth sports into a rich kid's game.
I know this isn't the first email I've sent on youth sports. I talk about it all the time. And people ask: why Chris, why do you talk about this so often?
This isn't just some sector of the economy, we are talking about access for kids to play sports. Did you play? Do you remember running around outside and having fun with friends?
How about if you are a parent or grandparent today? How important is that to you when you consider the alternative to that time playing outside is often the iPad and social media garbage?
It's locking far too many kids out ... and if private equity gets their way, far too many kids will grow up hitting a baseball like Vivek Ramaswamy.
That's why I introduced the Let Kids Play Act: to go right after the vulture investors and their practices pricing families out. When it comes to youth sports, we do not have to accept only corporate profits mattering.

To all VoteVets supporters: Please, don’t scroll past this.
We’re interrupting your Sunday morning to humbly ask you to make a contribution.
Of all VoteVets supporters, just 1% make a donation. Many think they’ll contribute later and forget. Many make a mental note and move on.
But right now, VoteVets is closing out the largest midterm campaign we have ever run. The GOP is on the ropes, they’re doing everything they can to compromise our elections and tear our candidates down. But if we do not meet the moment, all bets are off.
If everyone reading this email right now chipped in as little as $2, we’d crush our fundraising goals. We’d have enough to run our operations indefinitely. We could redouble our efforts to reach, persuade, and turn out Veterans in these final weeks. They are the key to this election.
But not everyone donates. That’s why it’s so important that you do, if you can.

Peter,

On September 30, every federal campaign in America has to close its books
and tally up how much we fundraised and how much cash we have left to
spend.

Then that report is filed with the Federal Election Commission, and it’s
made public for all to see. Reporters read it. MAGA billionaire donors
read it. Mike Rogers' people read it.

They’ll all be looking for the same thing: whether this campaign has the
money to stay on the air and remain competitive through November.

To put us in the best possible position heading into the final stretch,
I’m setting a goal of raising an additional $5 million before September
30. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260920-1-ak.ekfD98&amount=10&refcode=em20260920-3233&t=1004&akid=3243%2E251025%2Ee3vRmc ]If you can pitch in a few bucks to help us chip away at that goal,
I’d be so grateful. Even $10 makes a difference when tens of
thousands of you step up.

It's an ambitious goal. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

But look at what we're up against: Mike Rogers is Donald Trump's
handpicked candidate, a career politician with over $70 million in
commitments from Trump, Elon Musk, and GOP Super PACs.

They’re not playing it safe. We can’t either.

Peter, what
happens in Michigan will determine who wins the Senate majority.

The latest polls show this race is neck-and-neck.

Winning this race isn’t possible if we miss the mark in moments like this.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260920-1-ak.ekfD98&amount=10&refcode=em20260920-3233&t=1005&akid=3243%2E251025%2Ee3vRmc ]That’s why I’m humbly asking for your support today. Can you donate

contribution gives us the resources we need to fight back and win.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

subject: We are taking proactive steps to defend our democracy and secure our elections.

body:
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/]

Hi friend,

At the Republican Midterm Convention last week, President Trump tried to hawk his strategy for this election: handing out $5,000 checks if Republicans keep control of the House and Senate. Let us call this what it is: a transparent attempt to buy an election and distract from systemic political corruption and a failing economy.

While everyday families struggle with the squeezing cost of housing, groceries, and health care, the Trump Administration is treating governance like a pay-to-play scheme. But we are not just watching this happen from the sidelines. We are taking proactive steps to safeguard our democracy and hold Washington accountable.

In Congress, I am combating President Trump’s agenda by pushing for the passage of the Freedom to Vote Act and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to protect ballot access. I am also fighting to pass the Restore Trust in Government Act to ban stock trading for politicians — members of Congress and the President alike — because our elections should be decided by working families, not self-serving interests.

We need a House majority that will defend election integrity, protect our democratic institutions, and put working people first. Taking back the House starts right here in MD-03, but we cannot counter the Trump Administration's bribery without your support.

Will you chip in $5, $10, or $15 today to power our campaign push, fight back against President Trump's rhetoric, and defend our democracy? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-RepubMidterm?&refcode=E31690-20260920-RepubMidtermResend-SL-Resend&amount=5]

-Sarah Elfreth
https://elfrethformaryland.com/ [https://elfrethformaryland.com/] https://www.facebook.com/SarahforMD [https://www.facebook.com/SarahforMD] https://www.instagram.com/SarahforMaryland [https://www.instagram.com/SarahforMaryland] https://x.com/SarahforMD [https://x.com/SarahforMD]
Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her fiancé, Eric, and their dog, Ollie.
